title: Vermont Man Is Facing Felony OUI Charges After Crash In North Adams Sends Four People To The Hospital - WUPE
content: Ever wonder how much driving under the influence can impact someone and others? This is a perfect example. What started off as a normal Saturday afternoon turned into total chaos on Curran Highway in North Adams. As you know, Curran Highway is no exception when it comes to vehicle accidents. Only this time, it all could've been avoided if one driver hadn't been intoxicated. Charles Cairns, 57, of Brattleboro, Vermont, is facing felony charges for alleged drunken driving. What makes it a felony is the fact that this is his third drunken-driving offense. According to North Adams Police Chief Mark Bailey, police, firefighters, and Northern Berkshire EMS responded around 2:40 p.m. on Saturday, October 10, 2026, to a two-car crash near Duke’s Lumber, at 1526 Curran Highway. The Berkshire Eagle reports that Cairns was driving a Toyota Corolla south on Curran Highway when it collided with another southbound Dodge Ram carrying four people. Unfortunately, the Dodge Ram flipped onto its side, and all four occupants were taken to Berkshire Medical Center in Pittsfield for treatment. On Tuesday morning, Bailey said he didn’t know how seriously the occupants were injured and that Cairns had not been taken to the hospital. Cairns is charged with a third offense of operating under the influence and operating a motor vehicle under the influence with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or greater while causing serious bodily injury. Both charges are felonies in Massachusetts. He is being arraigned on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at Northern Berkshire District Court.

title: Prediction: A $1,000 Investment in TSMC Stock Will More Than Double by 2030. Here’s Why You Should Buy It Before Oct. 15. - The Motley Fool
content: TSMC's Oct. 15 earnings report could supercharge the stock and send it on a bull run through the end of the decade. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM +0.17%), popularly known as TSMC, has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global chip boom, primarily due to its position as the largest semiconductor foundry that manufactures chips for major consumer electronics companies and chip designers that serve multiple end markets. TSMC has capitalized on the artificial intelligence (AI) boom in recent years, thanks mainly to its advanced process nodes, which enable customers to manufacture cutting-edge chips. Not surprisingly, TSMC stock has gained nearly 384% over the past three years, outperforming the 246% gain in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index over the same period. I won't be surprised to see this semiconductor stock head higher after it releases its third-quarter results on Oct. 15. Let's look at the reasons why TSMC is primed for more upside, potentially doubling by 2030. This has been a strong year for TSMC. The company's revenue has increased by 41% in the first nine months of 2026, suggesting it is on track to exceed its 2025 revenue growth of 36%. Notably, TSMC's revenue growth has accelerated in recent months. Its September revenue increased nearly 55% from the same month in 2025, while August 2026 revenue was up by 53% over the same month last year. TSMC's Q3 revenue increased by 50% from the same period last year to $46.71 billion, beating estimates and exceeding the company's guidance range of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion. What's more, the company's net profit is expected to increase by 64% from the year-ago period, as noted by Reuters. In fact, Reuters points out that TSMC is on track to report its sixth consecutive quarter of record profits due to the huge investments in AI infrastructure. The good part is that the AI infrastructure boom is far from over. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you’d invested $5,000 then, you’d be sitting on $2,941,927 today.* Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It’s a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. Nvidia, for instance, expects to double its chip sales next year. On the other hand, Advanced Micro Devices expects it can substantially boost supply in 2027, as it sees strong demand for advanced chips driven by AI. Both Nvidia and AMD are TSMC's customers. As a result, it is easy to see why TSMC is reportedly planning to increase the production capacity of its advanced chip nodes next year. Market research firm TrendForce reports that TSMC's 2-nanometer (nm) chip production capacity could jump 22% by mid-2027 compared to the end of 2026. Additionally, the semiconductor giant is reportedly planning a 16% increase in 3nm production capacity over the same period. TSMC gets a third of its revenue from these two process nodes, so higher production bodes well for the company's performance next year. Also, TSMC is reportedly set to increase prices for its advanced nodes by 5%-10% next year, according to Taiwan's national news agency. So, TSMC should ideally witness a strong increase in both volumes and margins in 2027, which should allow it to sustain its robust revenue and earnings growth. Moreover, I won't be surprised to see TSMC offer a stronger-than-expected outlook when it reports results on Oct. 15, as AI customers such as Nvidia and AMD build up inventory to meet strong end-market demand. TSMC's sunny guidance could pave the way for more upside. Moreover, TSMC increased its global semiconductor revenue forecast for 2030 to $1.5 trillion in May this year, up from the earlier estimate of $1 trillion. So, the strong jump in TSMC's revenue and earnings is sustainable beyond 2027, and that's what analysts are expecting. The reason why I say this is that analysts have become quite bullish about TSMC's earnings growth prospects this year. Specifically, TSMC's earnings are anticipated to increase by 60% in 2026 to $17.04 per share. The forecast for the next couple of years points to solid 30% increases. TSM EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts Assuming TSMC's bottom line increases by even 20% in 2029 and 2030, its earnings per share could hit $42.05 by the end of the decade. If TSMC trades at 30 times earnings at that time, a slight discount to the Nasdaq-100 index's earnings multiple of 31.5, its stock price could reach $1,261. That's 184% higher than where TSMC stock is right now. So, a $1,000 investment in TSMC could be worth more than $2,800 in 2030, which is why investors should consider buying this multibagger stock before it soars higher following its Oct. 15 report. title: Why Did NVDA, TSM, WBD Stocks Hit 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) and Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. (WBD) hit fresh 52-week highs on Monday as investors piled into AI infrastructure and media consolidation plays. Higher Wall Street expectations for Nvidia, potential Musk-linked chipmaking plans at TSMC and WBD’s merger progress fueled the gains. Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor stocks gained over 2%, while Warner Bros. Discovery stock ended the session 0.03% higher. Nvidia stock surged to a record high of $240.10 as BNP Paribas issued a more bullish outlook, raising its price target to $345 from $285 while maintaining an ‘Outperform’ rating. The new price target implies a 44% upside to Monday’s close. The firm sees Nvidia's combination of CUDA software, NVLink networking and Blackwell processors as a competitive advantage as demand shifts toward AI inference workloads. Nvidia is a major player in the AI boom, supported by record sales and profits. It is also expanding its reach by investing in AI companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock jumped to ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’ territory the previous day. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing stock also reached an all-time high of $487.47 amid discussions involving Elon Musk's proposed Terafab semiconductor initiative. Under the potential arrangement, TSMC could develop and run a dedicated manufacturing operation for companies including Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Musk confirmed that discussions are taking place but cautioned that no agreement has been finalized, writing on X, “Just discussions, but something may come of it.” Retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory the previous day. Warner Bros. Discovery stock climbed to a four-year high of $30.99 as its combination with Paramount Skydance (PSKY) moved into its final operational stage. The transition marks a major change for the entertainment company following months of deal-related uncertainty. Incoming Chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz have outlined the leadership structure for the combined business. Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will oversee film operations, while Casey Bloys will continue leading direct-to-consumer streaming. James Gunn and Peter Safran will remain in charge of DC Studios. Retail sentiment remained ‘bullish’. So far this year, NVDA, TSM and WBD stocks have gained between 7% and 60%. The Nasdaq Composite led the climb, hitting an all-time high during trading hours and ending the session 1.05% up. She said that while intraday implied volatility has increased, the recent moves have yet to reach the extreme levels that preceded the 2022 equity bear market. As stocks rise to record levels and yields climb simultaneously, “my view is: don’t own bonds, with the exception of one-year Treasury bills, which are now at 4.55 percent,” he said. (CEG): The nuclear power company rose more than 3% overnight on Monday after a report suggested that it is close to a multi-year power deal with Google parent Alphabet valued at about $1 billion. Federal energy officials announced a conditional $4.2 billion loan commitment Monday to modernize and boost power production across nuclear generation facilities in Pennsylvania and Ohio, targeting rising regional electricity costs and surging energy demand. The funding, extended by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to Texas-based utility operator Vistra (VST), aims to expand generation capacity across existing facilities without necessitating new power transmission infrastructure. According to department officials, the initiative supports executive measures to bolster domestic nuclear infrastructure and restore American energy output. The planned upgrades focus on Vistra’s Beaver Valley plant in Pennsylvania, along with the Davis-Besse and Perry facilities in Ohio. By executing thermodynamic and hardware uprates, the project will add 433 megawatts of power capacity while maintaining nearly 4 gigawatts of steady baseload electricity—enough to supply power to more than 3 million households. Earlier in January this year, Meta Platforms (META) struck 20-year agreements to buy power from Vistra’s Perry and Davis-Besse plants in Ohio and Beaver Valley plant in Pennsylvania. Beyond expanding immediate output, the modernization strategy will help extend operational life cycles at the three Midwestern plants by up to 20 years beyond their current licensing terms. The conditional loan arrangement also leaves open an option to fund future uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak facility in Texas. Construction, engineering, and specialized maintenance during scheduled outage periods are projected to support about 3,000 temporary jobs while protecting thousands of permanent operational positions at the facilities. By boosting generation within established facility footprints, the funding addresses growing power consumption across the 13-state PJM Interconnection grid, which serves major industrial and residential centers throughout the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions. Final disbursement of the $4.2 billion loan remains contingent on Vistra meeting mandatory environmental, legal, technical, and financial criteria required by federal regulators. One of 2026’s biggest investment winners does not own technology stocks, cryptocurrency or even crude oil. However, it does track the cost of getting oil onto a ship and through increasingly dangerous waters. The Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (BWET) has surged 2,928% this year as months of disruption around the Strait of Hormuz sent freight costs soaring, eclipsing even leveraged bets on semiconductor and energy stocks. BWET’s year-to-date percentage gain is nearly 12 times the 244% advance in the MicroSectors U.S. Big Oil Index 3X ETN (NRGU) and almost 15 times the 199% rise in the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares ETF (SOXL). Other strong energy performers lag far behind. The MicroSectors Oil & Gas Exploration & Production 3X Leveraged ETN (OILU) has gained about 148%, while the Direxion Daily S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production Bull 2X Shares ETF (GUSH) has risen 119%. Among semiconductor ETFs, the First Trust Nasdaq Semiconductor ETF (FTXL) has advanced 82% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) about 77%. The S&P 500, tracked by SPY, had gained 12% through Wednesday, while the Nasdaq Composite was up 13%. BWET has also dwarfed the wider energy rally. Its 2,928% gain is about 19 times WTI crude’s 151% advance, 25 times the United States Oil Fund (USO) 's 117% return, and 61 times the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) 's 48% gain. Launched in May 2023, BWET is a specialized commodity-pool ETF that holds near-dated crude-tanker freight futures rather than oil, shipping stocks, or physical vessels. Its exposure is concentrated in the Baltic Exchange’s TD3C route: very large crude carriers hauling oil from the Middle East Gulf to China. A smaller allocation tracks Suezmax shipments from West Africa to Europe. The Gulf-to-China route passes through Hormuz, making the fund particularly sensitive to the availability of ships willing to cross the strait. Higher freight futures can lift BWET even when oil prices fall. Conversely, an easing of shipping constraints can hurt the fund without requiring a comparable decline in crude. The disruption began after the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February when Tehran effectively closed Hormuz to most commercial traffic. Before the war, about 125 large commercial ships crossed daily. Gulf supertanker hire rates were around $75,000 to $100,000 a day. By late June, tanker rates for voyages through Hormuz had surged to nearly $470,000 a day, while rates outside the strait jumped to $190,500 from $106,500 in just one week. The problem wasn't just demand for oil. Ships were stranded, owners were refusing voyages, and the vessels available to carry remaining cargo commanded exceptional prices. Insurance is another hurdle. At the APPEC industry conference on Wednesday, Emirates National Oil Company (ENOC) said transit costs ran from $10 million to $20 million per voyage, and cargo-insurance bills hit nearly $10 million. Additional war-risk coverage for leaving the Gulf, previously negligible, could reach “10 percent of the cargo.” BWET does not track insurance costs directly. However, higher war-risk premiums can discourage ships from entering the Gulf, tighten available capacity and increase the freight rates underlying the fund’s futures. June briefly offered a way out. The U.S. lifted its blockade of Iranian ports on June 18 under an agreement that promised 60 days of toll-free passage and the restoration of commercial traffic within 30 days. Some stranded tankers escaped. But mines, rival transit corridors and renewed attacks kept the route far from normal. Middle East-to-China VLCC rates fell to about $287,000 a day by June 30 from more than $500,000 before the peace announcement. The ceasefire subsequently broke down, and Washington reimposed its blockade in mid-July. BWET had already shown how quickly diplomacy could reverse the trade. The ETF fell about 13% at the open on April 9 after Iran said it would allow safe passage, then rebounded when tanker traffic was halted again. The latest round of violence has further narrowed the pool of willing operators. U.S. forces said they destroyed five Iranian crude tankers on Tuesday following attempted missile attacks on an American warship, after striking three tankers days earlier. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard separately claimed attacks on two U.S. vessels and eight oil tankers. The violence has also threatened shuttle vessels carrying Gulf crude to larger tankers waiting outside Hormuz, which is a workaround to keep risk-averse ships away from the strait. Only six tracked commodity ships crossed the strait on Tuesday, far below the 125 daily transits recorded before the war. The tally excludes vessels operating with tracking systems switched off, but major shipping companies are reluctant to return. Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Japan’s second-largest shipping company with a fleet of more than 900 vessels, said normal operations were unlikely to resume soon. CEO Jotaro Tamura said it was “difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year.” On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for BWET flipped dramatically to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘extremely bearish’ levels three months ago amid a 900% surge in message volume over the past month. It will dramatically decline in price when the war ends or another fake ceasefire but right now it just keeps climbing.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. The transaction comes as American investors and defense companies increasingly target Ukraine’s combat-proven unmanned technology. The country has developed a large drone ecosystem during its war with Russia, but hundreds of businesses now compete for military demand, said the report. Swarmer U.S. CEO Alex Fink said many Ukrainian businesses lack the infrastructure needed to expand internationally and therefore need partners that can provide funding and access to overseas markets. Prince, who serves as Swarmer’s chairman, said the company intends to pursue additional acquisitions and partnerships involving defense and security technologies that have already demonstrated their value in combat. Swarmer has been developing counter-drone systems, including swarming drone interceptors. Its recent partnership with Vectus Air Defense Systems, a new company led by Erik Prince will provide customized air-defense services to governments and critical infrastructure operators. The second quarter marked Swarmer’s first full quarter as a public company. Swarmer reported Q2 2026 revenue of $216,413, up 56%. Gross margin more than doubled to $183,597. However, operating expenses surged to $7.5 million from $854,847, driven by higher investments in personnel, engineering, product development and public-company costs. Net loss widened to $7.3 million from $1.6 million. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ the previous day. content: U.S. stock futures were under pressure early on Thursday as rising Treasury yields, oil prices and fresh questions about the scale and financing of the artificial-intelligence investment boom kept traders on the edge. As of 4:00 a.m. ET, Dow futures fell 0.6%, Nasdaq futures declined 0.5%, S&P 500 futures were down 0.3%, and Russell 2000 futures fell 0.9%. The early weakness follows a softer Wednesday session. 30-year Treasury yields touched 24-year highs, and the September FOMC minutes signaled another potential rate hike before year-end. However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500 Index, and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, has stayed ‘extremely bullish.’ Meanwhile, President Donald Trump will attend a White House summit today to host top technology leaders in Washington and announce $1B+ in industry commitments for the Genesis Mission. He will also award the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AMD CEO Lisa Su, and Google co-founder Sergey Brin. Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Broadcom (AVGO): Shares dipped over 1% in early premarket. Reports revealed it is seeking over $50 billion in financing for OpenAI’s custom AI chip development and Oracle’s cloud infrastructure deployment. Micron Technology (MU), Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM): Shares fell over 1% in early premarket despite TSMC posting a 54.6% YoY jump in September revenue. It is expected to provide its full quarterly results and a detailed AI-demand outlook next week. Meanwhile, Samsung has signaled a record $80 billion operating profit. Separately, Micron has also agreed to pay $600 million to license Netlists’ (NLST) patents and settle ongoing litigation. Microsoft (MSFT) is on the retail radar after a four-day winning streak, following the opening of preorders for the Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra and the announcement of local AI model integration into Windows. Amazon (AMZN): Reports indicate nearly 1,000 job cuts primarily within its Stores e-commerce unit amid ongoing corporate cost-cutting. Wolfspeed (WOLF): Shares soared 18% in early premarket trade after securing a conditional 30-year, $1.5 billion loan commitment from the U.S. Department of War to expand domestic radiation-hardened chip production. Applied Digital (APLD): The AI data-center operator reported a sharp revenue increase in Q1, along with a new agreement securing up to 1 gigawatt of power capacity in Finland. IonQ (IONQ): Gained momentum after advancing to the final stage of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (worth up to $300 million through 2029) to validate utility-scale quantum fabrication. SpaceX (SPCX) remains one of the most watched names as the FCC prepares to consider new spectrum rules that could accelerate satellite-to-smartphone services. SpaceX and Amazon are among the companies positioned to benefit. Separately, Jim Cramer said that SpaceX could become Nvidia’s largest customer. Keep an eye on Rocket Lab (RKLB) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) as well. Tesla (TSLA): Heading for a weekly win as Dan Ives initiated coverage with a $500 price target, citing over 30% upside from software and physical AI. UBS also raised its target to $391. Kratos Defense (KTOS), Aerovironment (AVAV): In the spotlight as Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest added significant shares in both companies following increased Pentagon focus on autonomous drone warfare. Robinhood (HOOD), Webull (BULL): Webull stock plunged on Wednesday after a bipartisan House panel flagged national security concerns over its China ties. Robinhood and Public moved aggressively to poach Webull clients by offering 3% transfer bonuses. Skydance Media (SKYD): Reports indicate that David Ellison and his family contributed approximately $17 billion toward the $110 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. transaction. Lululemon (LULU): Facing pressure toward a second weekly decline despite overhauling its senior leadership team to reignite top-line growth. The company appointed Maggie Gauger as President and Chief Product Officer and Joseph Godsey as Chief Operating Officer, while searches are underway for new brand, communications and technology chiefs. ImmunityBio (IBRX): Under pressure and heading for its worst week in over two months despite management highlighting new coverage linkages with Aetna-CVS. Sellas Life Sciences (SLS): Retail traders analyzed new acute myeloid leukemia (AML) comparative trial data published in Nature. Other tickers trending on Stocktwits at the time of writing included Sea Ltd (SE), Baidu Inc (BIDU), D-Wave Quantum (QBTS), and Cipher Digital (CIFR). What Else To Watch On ThursdayOn the economic front, traders will watch the release of weekly jobless claims at 8:30 am ET, followed by wholesale trade data at 9:00 am ET. The Fed's September meeting minutes showed that most officials see another rate increase as possible before year-end. (APLD) shares jumped nearly 5% in early premarket trading on Thursday after the AI data center operator reported fiscal first-quarter results that comfortably topped Wall Street expectations, with revenue surging more than fourfold year over year. Revenue for the quarter ended August jumped 322% to $341.9 million from $80.9 million a year earlier, well above the $116.3 million analysts polled by FactSet expected. Adjusted net loss narrowed to $0.01 per diluted share from $0.03 a year earlier, also beating expectations for a $0.30 loss. However, some of the more interesting disclosures came during management’s earnings call. CEO Wes Cummins said on the analyst call that Applied Digital is aware of a roughly 1-gigawatt self-build project being developed by a Tier 1 hyperscaler in the state, separate from the three customer projects Applied Digital already has there. “We’re aware of a self-build project, roughly 1 gigawatt self-build project from one of the Tier 1 hyperscalers in the state as well. And we’ve been – that is outside of the ones that we already have in the state,” Cummins said. Cummins added that Applied Digital is also in discussions with multiple hyperscaler customers for additional capacity in North Dakota, highlighting the state’s growing importance as an AI data center hub. Overall, the company expects to bring more than 600 MW online over the next 12 months and sees potential to reach 3.5 GW to 4 GW of operating capacity by the end of 2030, Cummins said. Applied Digital began locking in key components nearly two years ago. In some cases, it went much further by effectively reserving entire manufacturing outputs. “In some of those instances, we actually purchased full factory capacity output from certain factories for, I believe, a 4-year time frame to make sure that we had those key components locked in,” Cummins said. He said the company is now looking to increase those commitments as it anticipates stronger demand for components through 2027, 2028 and 2029. APLD was the top trending stock on Stocktwits as of early Thursday, with retail sentiment shifting to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish.’ “$APLD bought 1 million more today, and bot is set to buy all week. huge beats,” a trader said, while another wrote, “$APLD upgrades and gap up tomorrow.” Applied Digital has lagged the broader AI infrastructure boom, with its shares down 3% year-to-date as of the last close. (IBRX) remained under pressure this week even as founder Patrick Soon-Shiong touted a cancer-care initiative linking his separate NantIQ tech business with insurer Aetna, part of CVS Health, fueling retail hopes for indirect benefits to the biotech firm. IBRX stock rose 0.6% on Wednesday to $9.75 but remained down 5% for the week, putting it on track for its worst weekly performance since late July. In a post on X, Soon-Shiong outlined integrating imaging, immunotherapy, chemotherapy and radiation so doctors could coordinate cancer treatment more precisely. “That day has arrived thanks to Aetna CVS and our amazing tech/AI team at NantIQ,” he said, identifying NantIQ as another NantWorks company. The connection runs through Soon-Shiong: he founded ImmunityBio, which develops and commercializes immunotherapies, while NantIQ is a separate tech business within his broader NantWorks network. Aetna, the insurer owned by CVS Health, uses Eviti in parts of its cancer-treatment authorization process. Soon-Shiong highlighted Eviti, which he called “Evidence-Based Treatment Integration,” as a platform in development for a decade. He also pointed to “Trial Match” as the next step, aiming to help doctors and patients learn about advanced clinical trials. Aetna announced last month that it expanded bundled prior authorizations to eligible Medicaid members across all cancer types, effective Sept. 1. Rather than requiring separate approvals for individual services, the approach lets providers submit a broader treatment plan through one portal. Depending on the plan, that can include chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation, and related MRI or CT scans. Aetna said providers previously submitted an average of four separate authorization requests for these services. Nearly a quarter of eligible members were already receiving care under bundled approvals. The insurer plans to expand the approach across its businesses next year, including Medicare and commercial plans during the first half of the year. Meanwhile, Eviti checks proposed cancer-treatment plans against clinical evidence and insurance policies before treatment begins. The NantIQ update builds on Soon-Shiong’s push for ‘Immunotherapy 2.0,’ combining treatments, diagnostics and immune monitoring to prevent cancer from returning. After welcoming Michael Caputo’s appointment to Trump’s Cancer Panel, he said, “We are closer than ever.” ImmunityBio’s flagship immunotherapy, Anktiva, received FDA approval in April 2024 for use with BCG in certain patients with bladder cancer that has not responded to BCG treatment. The next major milestone is the FDA’s Jan. 6, 2027, target decision date on expanding Anktiva’s bladder-cancer label to papillary-only disease. Anktiva is already approved in the U.S. for carcinoma in situ, with or without papillary tumors, while July’s UAE authorization expanded its regulatory footprint to 34 countries. (NIO) are poised to end a five-week losing streak as Onvo crosses 200,000 cumulative deliveries and battery swaps hit a fresh holiday record, giving retail bulls fresh milestones to weigh against persistent sales pressure. Nio’s U.S.-listed shares rose 2% in the previous session to $3.54, and are up 5% through Wednesday. Onvo marked its 200,000th delivery on Thursday, handing over a flagship L90 SUV to the family of Chinese television host Geng Chenchen. The family-focused brand reached the milestone roughly two years after L60 deliveries began in September 2024. Its lineup now includes three electric SUVs: the L60, L80 and L90, CnEVPost noted. Onvo ended September with 198,760 cumulative deliveries, implying it delivered another 1,240 vehicles this month. China’s Oct.1-Oct.7 National Day holiday typically slows automotive production and handovers. The cumulative milestone comes against weaker recent sales. Onvo delivered 8,763 vehicles in September, down 43% from a year earlier and 0.5% from August, marking its fourth consecutive monthly decline. Third-quarter deliveries fell 26% from a year ago to 27,728. Deliveries across the first nine months were nearly flat at 70,191, up just 1%. While Onvo works to rebuild sales momentum, Nio’s swapping network saw record holiday demand. The company completed 183,664 battery swaps on Monday, up from 183,469 on Oct. 1. The new peak was 4.4% above February’s Lunar New Year record and 7.7% above the May 1 total, EV reported. Across the network, that equates to roughly one completed swap every 0.47 seconds. “For long-distance driving, swapping is the first choice,” Nio said on Weibo. The holiday peaks underscore the role of highway infrastructure for drivers making longer journeys. Nio said its highway swapping network connects more than 550 cities and allows drivers to reach every provincial-level region of mainland China using swap stations. Nio’s network map showed 4,165 swap stations in China on Wednesday, including 1,072 on highways. It also listed 5,376 charging stations with 31,005 charging piles. Cumulative swaps exceeded 127 million, while charging sessions passed 100 million. Drivers of other brands accounted for 86.7% of the energy delivered by Nio’s own chargers, according to the map. The company still faces a substantial construction push to meet its target of adding 1,000 swap stations this year. With 489 added so far, another 511 would need to open before year-end, requiring 5.9 openings a day. Partner funding could support that expansion. Geely Holding Group agreed last month to acquire a 30% stake in Nio Power in a deal valuing the charging and swapping business at approximately 16 billion yuan, or $2.4 billion. Nio’s longer-term target is 10,000 swap stations by 2030. Battery swapping is also part of Onvo’s pitch to family buyers. Its vehicles share Nio’s charging, swapping and service infrastructure, giving the brand access to the expanding network. Onvo refreshed the L90 in April, launched the five-seat L80 in May and updated the entry-level L60 in June. Selected variants feature Nio’s in-house Shenji NX9031 driver-assistance chip, LiDAR and the Nio World Model system. The brand added new design packages for the L80 and L90 in September and said pn Thursday that it now operates 374 service centers across 213 Chinese cities. Im ready to buy more!” Another trader said, “Been nibbling more on the slow momentum. 38,300 shares now.” A third user celebrated the recent rebound: “Thank you lord for the 3rd Green Day in a row. Let’s go!” Nio’s U.S.-listed shares have slumped 31% year-to-date. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. title: Why Is TSM Stock Rising Premarket? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. rose 0.6% in early premarket trading on Monday after the contract chipmaker’s monthly sales update showed continued robust demand for AI and chips. Revenue in July rose 45% to NT$467.58 billion ($14.5 billion). Analysts on average are estimating a 46.8% increase in sales for the current quarter, Q3. The latest performance shows steady demand for advanced chips, which power data centers and other systems that power AI applications, smartphones and automobiles. TSMC makes cutting-edge semiconductors for the likes of Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. The biggest buyers of those chips – including cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft – have set aside about $800 billion for AI-related investments this year. Last month, TSMC raised its spending and revenue projections for the year, reflecting confidence in demand for chips powering AI development. TSMC now expects its capital expenditure to reach a record level of $60 billion to $64 billion in 2026 and forecasts its full-year sales to grow slightly above 40% in U.S. dollar terms. Separately, Sony Group and TSMC announced a plan to spend around ‌1 trillion yen ($6.32 billion) to jointly ‌make next-generation microchips used in image sensors, the Nikkei ​business daily said on Monday. A joint venture owned about 60% by Sony and 40% by TSMC will start commercial production as early ‌as 2029 in ⁠southern Japan's Kumamoto prefecture, the paper said. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for TSMC remained ‘bearish,’ unchanged from the previous day, with several users posting about the monthly update. TSM stock gained nearly 4% last week and is up 39% year to date. In comparison, the semiconductor benchmark iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) has increased nearly 80% over the past year. title: The Giant White Pyramid Overlooking Phoenix - K101
content: Over the weekend, I took a trip to Phoenix. While up there, I stumbled across one of the state's strangest landmarks. Standing among the red rocks of Papago Park was a giant white pyramid that seemed completely out of place. As it turns out, the mysterious structure marks the grave of Arizona's first governor, George Hunt. George Wiley Paul Hunt was Arizona's first state governor. He was born in 1859 and initially moved to Arizona in search of gold. However, instead of staking a claim at a mine, he got into politics. He was elected Globe's first mayor in 1904 and served for many years on the Arizona Territorial Council and in the Arizona Territorial Legislature. In 1910, Hunt was a part of the Arizona Constitutional Convention, and in 1911, he was elected state governor. George Hunt served 7 terms as governor before passing away in 1934; he was buried at the Papago Park Cemetery, alongside his wife Helen. READ: How Doc Holliday Became A Legend In The American West George Hunt commissioned a pyramid to be made for his wife, Helen, who had passed away from Appendicitis in 1931. He had been inspired by the ancient pyramids he had seen during his travels, and he wanted a monument that would endure for generations. Construction on the monument was completed the following year, creating an unusual family mausoleum overlooking Papago Park. Helen was the first person entombed there, and when Hunt died in 1934, he was laid to rest beside her. Other members of the family, including the Hunts' daughter, Virginia, and several of Helen's relatives, were also buried within the pyramid. RELATED: Who Was Big Nose Kate And Why Is She Famous? Many people know of Governor George Hunt for his unusual resting place, but his true legacy lies in the shaping of early Arizona.  As the state's first governor, he guided Arizona through its infancy by advocating for critical reforms, including women’s suffrage, workers' compensation, public education, and old-age pensions. Although Hunt's Tomb is Arizona's most famous pyramid, it is not the state's only pyramid-shaped monument. Arizona is also home to the Hi Jolly Monument in Quartzsite, a pyramid-shaped memorial dedicated to Hadji Ali, better known as Hi Jolly. Hi Jolly was one of the camel drivers brought to the American Southwest during the U.S. Army's Camel Corps experiment. When he passed away, a pyramid was built over his grave. Another notable Pyramid Tomb in Arizona is the pyramid tomb of Charles Debrille Poston, often called the "Father of Arizona." His monument can be found near Florence. Poston built this pyramid in the 1870's as a religious symbol. In 1925, on what would've been his 100th birthday, his remains were moved inside the pyramid. READ MORE ABOUT THE CAMEL CORPS: Arizona Camel Corps: The Army’s Desert Experiment Governor Hunt's Tomb is recognized as a historic landmark and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2008, cementing its place as an important piece of Arizona history. Today, visitors can enjoy a short hike to his monument, take in panoramic views of Phoenix, and learn more about the man who helped guide Arizona through its earliest years as a state. Hunt wanted a tomb that would endure for generations, and judging by the number of people who still stop to look at it in awe, he got his wish. For years, the race to build better artificial intelligence centered on making models bigger, feeding them more data, and expanding the amount of information they could process at once. Now, a fresh frontier is emerging as researchers increasingly explore smarter memory management as another way to build more capable AI systems. Two academic papers published this month, AutoMem and SelfMem, argue that memory shouldn't be a rigid feature engineered by developers using static rules. Instead, they propose that AI systems can learn to manage their own memories. They take different approaches: AutoMem trains AI to manage an external memory system, while SelfMem lets agents refine their own memory strategies through feedback, and both report substantial gains on long-horizon benchmarks. Imagine working with an AI coding assistant on a project for months. Instead of repeatedly reminding it about your project's architecture and coding style, a smarter memory system could retain the decisions that matter while discarding obsolete information. Researchers believe that this kind of selective memory will become increasingly important as AI agents take on longer-running tasks. One way developers have tried to build more capable chatbots is by expanding their context windows, which are the immediate digital scratchpad an AI considers during a conversation. While larger context windows let models process more information, they also increase computational costs and don't necessarily help AI distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. The papers instead explore an alternative approach based on active memory curation. In AutoMem, Stanford University researchers introduced a memory manager that decides when to create, update, search, and delete records, allowing the AI to maintain a compact memory instead of continuously accumulating information. Tested on grueling, complex video games like NetHack and Crafter, this memory-management approach slashed the agent's memory growth rate by 95% and doubled its task performance, allowing a 32-billion-parameter open-weight model to perform competitively with frontier models including Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking on the evaluated long-horizon benchmarks. SelfMem takes a completely parameter-free approach. Instead of editing model weights, it gives the AI a dedicated workspace and tools to inspect an unchangeable transcript store. It allows the agent to inspect, write, review, and revise its own memory, outperforming traditional retrieval pipelines by more than 40% on the BEAM benchmark while using only a fraction of the computational cost. The push for smarter memory comes as AI companies shift from one-off chatbots to autonomous agents designed to work over days or weeks. Whether writing software, tracking supply chains, or managing research projects, these systems must retain relevant information while discarding details that no longer matter. That is where autonomous memory management changes the equation. Instead of forcing a user to repeatedly copy-paste instructions, an agent equipped with an optimized memory workflow seamlessly recalls structural boundaries, tracks cumulative progress, and discards transient data that is no longer relevant. Better memory could also reduce the computational cost of repeatedly processing the same information, a potential advantage as AI companies look to deploy agents more efficiently at scale. Over the past year, leading AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic have introduced basic memory features, allowing consumer chatbots to retain user preferences and custom instructions across distinct chat sessions. Today's commercial memory features generally rely on predefined mechanisms for deciding what information is retained. AutoMem and SelfMem instead point toward AI systems capable of independently evaluating and regulating their own memories. As tech companies race to build AI systems capable of executing truly long-horizon work, the findings suggest memory management may become an increasingly important complement to larger models. Future AI systems may be judged not only by how much they know, but also by how effectively they decide what information is worth keeping. Share-market pricing can reflect expectations concerning AI-related demand, production capacity, technological progress, and the pace at which capital spending translates into additional output. These factors do not necessarily develop at the same rate. Revenue growth can coincide with substantial investment in new facilities, limiting near-term free cash flow even when manufacturing activity expands. Taiwan remains central to the companys manufacturing network. The concentration of advanced semiconductor production in a particular geographic area connects manufacturing continuity with local infrastructure, electricity availability, water supplies, logistics, and cross-border trade conditions. The company has also pursued manufacturing expansion outside Taiwan, including projects in the United States and Japan. Overseas facilities involve different construction schedules, operating costs, workforce requirements, supplier networks, and public-sector arrangements. Establishing production in additional locations can diversify manufacturing capacity, although new facilities require time and substantial resources before reaching established operating levels. Geographic expansion also involves coordinating equipment installation, technical staffing, supplier access, and customer qualification procedures. Semiconductor production depends on specialised materials and equipment sourced through international supply chains, making coordination across multiple regions an important operational requirement. The S&P 500 provides broad context for US-listed equities, while semiconductor manufacturers operate within an industry shaped by technological development, capital intensity, and changing demand across computing markets. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturings business also serves customers and industries beyond the United States, so its operating performance cannot be explained solely through movements in a US equity benchmark. Developments in AI infrastructure, advanced packaging, manufacturing yields, and semiconductor fabrication technology remain relevant to the companys operating results. Electricity requirements, equipment availability, construction schedules, and the pace of customer product launches can also affect production and cash generation. Differences between projected cash flow and prevailing share-market pricing therefore depend on several variables rather than a single revenue measure. The S&P 500 remains a useful broad-market reference, while the companys manufacturing activity, capital expenditure, and cash conversion provide business-specific context. title: TSMC Earnings Preview: Can Record Revenue and AI Demand Push TSM Stock Higher? - Markets.com
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company will report third-quarter earnings on Thursday, October 15, with record revenue already confirmed and investor attention shifting toward profitability, artificial intelligence demand and the company’s outlook for the final quarter of 2026. TSMC’s US-listed shares ended Friday at approximately $453.31 after declining about 1%. The stock remains close to recent highs, reflecting confidence that spending by Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and major cloud companies will continue driving demand for advanced chips. However, elevated expectations create a demanding setup. With third-quarter sales already known, stronger margins and an upbeat forecast may be necessary to push TSM stock decisively higher. TSMC will hold its third-quarter earnings conference on Thursday, October 15, from 2:00 a.m. to 3:30 a.m. Eastern Time, corresponding to 2:00 p.m. in Taiwan. The results will therefore be available before the US stock market opens. TSMC entered its quiet period on October 5, preventing management from communicating with the investment community until the earnings release. The report will have implications well beyond TSM stock. As the world’s largest contract chipmaker, TSMC manufactures processors for many of the companies leading the AI investment cycle. Its capacity utilization, advanced-node demand and capital-spending plans can provide early signals for Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Apple and the wider semiconductor sector. The main revenue surprise arrived before the full earnings report. TSMC generated September revenue of NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% from a year earlier but down 0.6% from August. Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached NT$3.90 trillion, representing annual growth of 41.1%. Combined revenue for July, August and September reached approximately NT$1.49 trillion, equivalent to about $46.7 billion. That was roughly 51% higher than the NT$989.92 billion reported one year earlier. The result exceeded the NT$1.46 trillion estimate compiled from 19 analysts. It also came in above TSMC’s previous dollar-denominated guidance of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion. An LSEG SmartEstimate places third-quarter net profit at approximately NT$740.8 billion, which would represent growth of about 64% from the same quarter in 2025. TSMC occupies a central position in the AI supply chain because it manufactures the advanced processors designed by Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and other chip developers. Demand for AI accelerators has expanded beyond GPUs. Cloud companies and technology groups are increasingly developing custom application-specific chips for inference, networking and data processing. Many of these designs depend on TSMC’s leading manufacturing nodes and advanced packaging capacity. The company’s high-performance computing business accounted for approximately two-thirds of revenue during the second quarter. That category includes AI accelerators, data-center CPUs and other powerful processors. TSMC’s third-quarter revenue indicates that concerns about an immediate slowdown in AI infrastructure spending have not yet translated into weaker chip orders. September sales increased almost 55% from a year earlier even as investors questioned the sustainability of spending by hyperscale cloud companies. The key issue on the earnings call will be whether management believes current demand represents long-term deployment or accelerated purchasing caused by fears of capacity shortages. Investors will also look for updates on demand related to Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin platform, AMD’s accelerator roadmap and custom AI chips produced for major cloud providers. Revenue has already exceeded expectations, making profitability the most important unknown in the report. TSMC previously forecast a third-quarter gross margin between 65% and 67%, with an operating margin between 56% and 58%. Recent analyst estimates place the gross margin near 66.5%, toward the upper half of the company’s range. The comparison with the second quarter is demanding. TSMC reported: The second-quarter gross and operating margins exceeded the company’s original guidance, helped by high utilization, favorable product mix and cost improvements. The results also included a one-time investment gain, making the underlying sequential comparison less straightforward. Several factors could pressure margins in the third quarter. New overseas factories initially operate at higher costs than established Taiwanese facilities, while an accelerating 2-nanometer production ramp could create temporary inefficiencies. Foreign-exchange movements may also affect profitability because much of TSMC’s revenue is denominated in US dollars while a substantial portion of its costs is incurred in New Taiwan dollars. A gross margin above 67% would probably be viewed as a significant positive surprise. A result near the lower end of the company’s range could raise concerns that overseas expansion and advanced-node investments are absorbing more of the revenue benefit. Because quarterly revenue is already known, TSMC’s forecast for the final three months of the year may have a greater effect on its share price than the reported third-quarter numbers. Investors will want to see whether demand remains strong enough to produce another sequential revenue increase. Analysts expect Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform, expanding custom-chip production and the 2-nanometer ramp to support continued growth. Management’s full-year forecast will also be important. TSMC previously projected revenue growth of more than 40% for 2026 and increased its annual capital expenditure guidance to between $60 billion and $64 billion. Another increase in the revenue or capital-spending outlook would suggest that management continues to see demand exceeding available advanced manufacturing and packaging capacity. Investors should monitor four elements of the new guidance: The strongest scenario for TSM stock would combine better-than-expected margins with an increase in fourth-quarter revenue guidance. Strong sales accompanied by weaker margins or cautious 2027 commentary could produce a more subdued reaction. TSMC is investing aggressively outside Taiwan to meet customer and government demands for geographically diversified semiconductor production. Its expansion in Arizona is strategically important, but new overseas facilities generally carry higher construction, labor and operating costs. Management has previously acknowledged that overseas production will dilute company-wide margins, although pricing, subsidies and productivity improvements may offset part of the effect. TSMC must also fund the transition to more advanced technologies while expanding mature-node and packaging capacity. The scale of this investment helps strengthen its competitive position, but it increases execution risk if AI demand eventually slows. Export restrictions represent another uncertainty. Tighter controls on advanced chip sales to China could limit some orders, while changes in US tariff or semiconductor policy could affect investment decisions and customer supply chains. A bullish earnings outcome would probably require more than a headline revenue beat because record sales have already been disclosed. TSM stock could struggle if management forecasts slower sequential growth, warns about customer inventory or signals that overseas expansion will reduce margins more rapidly than expected. Valuation also raises the threshold for a positive surprise. TSM shares have risen substantially as investors priced in several years of AI-related growth. The stock’s decline following strong second-quarter results demonstrated that exceptional results can still disappoint when market expectations are even higher. TSM stock enters the report near $453, below the recent technical breakout area around $479. A return above that region could strengthen the bullish trend and place the recent highs back in focus. On the downside, the $450 area represents the first important support. A disappointing margin or outlook could push the stock toward the $430 to $440 region, particularly if Treasury yields remain elevated and pressure semiconductor valuations. The broader analyst outlook remains positive, although price-target estimates vary considerably. One compilation places the average target near $525, with forecasts ranging from $330 to $665. Third-quarter revenue reached a record NT$1.49 trillion and exceeded market expectations as AI accelerators, high-performance computing and advanced manufacturing continued to drive growth. The October 15 report will determine whether that revenue surge translated into equally strong earnings and margins. More importantly, investors will examine whether management expects the AI investment cycle to continue supporting record sales into 2027. TSM stock could extend its rally if TSMC reports a gross margin near or above 67% and issues another strong revenue forecast. However, elevated expectations mean that a routine earnings beat may not be sufficient. title: Earnings Week Ahead: JPM, JNJ, BAC, GS, C, UNH, TSM, and more - TradingView
content: The upcoming week marks the beginning of earnings season, with major U.S. banks, semiconductor leaders, healthcare companies, and asset managers taking center stage. JPMorgan Chase JPM, Bank of America BAC, Wells Fargo WFC, Citigroup C, Goldman Sachs GS, and Morgan Stanley MS headline the banking lineup, offering insight into lending trends, net interest income, trading activity, investment banking, and consumer credit quality. BlackRock BLK, Bank of New York Mellon BNY, and Interactive Brokers IBKR will add perspectives on asset flows, custody services, and investor activity. In technology, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM and ASML ASML will provide fresh signals on AI-driven chip demand, manufacturing capacity, and semiconductor equipment spending. Johnson & Johnson JNJ and UnitedHealth Group UNH bring healthcare into focus, while Alcoa AA offers a read on industrial demand. Prologis PLD, Domino’s Pizza DPZ, Fastenal FAST, Ericsson ERIC and Travelers TRV, alongside regional lenders U.S. Bancorp USB, Truist Financial TFC, PNC Financial Services PNC and M&T Bank MTB, round out a packed slate spanning logistics, consumer spending, business activity, insurance, and credit conditions. Below is a rundown of the major quarterly reports expected during the week of October 12–16. The week starts off relatively quiet, as there are no major earnings announcements planned. JPMorgan Chase JPM is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Tuesday, October 13, following a strong second quarter and upbeat management commentary on trading and investment banking activity. In Q2 2026, JPMorgan reported net income of $21.2B and EPS of $7.70, well above the $5.59 consensus, while managed revenue rose 27.7% Y/Y to $58.0B. Results included a $7.9B gain from the sale of Visa shares and a partial release of credit loss reserves. Excluding these items, EPS was $6.14, and return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) reached 23%. Following the quarter, management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for net interest income (NII) excluding Markets to approximately $96.5B, total NII to $105.5B, and adjusted expenses to $107.5B, while lowering its expected card net charge-off rate to approximately 3.2%. JPMorgan’s Q3 outlook has strengthened following comments from head of trading Troy Rohrbaugh in September that trading revenue and investment banking fees could each increase by a mid-to-high teens percentage Y/Y. This contrasts with Bank of America’s forecast for a decline of more than 10% in investment banking fees. On October 7, JPMorgan also announced the expansion of Chase Payroll, powered by Gusto, extending its business banking services for small and midsize businesses. Barclays maintained an Overweight rating and a $420 price target on October 6, forecasting Q3 operating EPS of $6.02 against consensus of approximately $5.90. The firm also expects JPMorgan to provide an initial 2027 NII forecast of around $103B. Options markets imply a potential move of approximately 4.4% in either direction following the results, above the 10-year average earnings-day move of 3.4%. Wall Street rates JPMorgan a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating is more cautious at Hold. Johnson & Johnson JNJ is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Tuesday, with recent pipeline developments across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience adding to the focus on its pharmaceutical growth outlook. In Q2 2026, Johnson & Johnson reported record revenue of $25.31B, up 6.6% Y/Y, while adjusted EPS of $2.90 topped the $2.84 consensus. Innovative Medicine sales reached $16.4B, up 7.8% operationally, supported by oncology drugs DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, ERLEADA, and RYBREVANT, while SPRAVATO sales rose 40.8% in Neuroscience. MedTech revenue increased 4.5% operationally to $8.9B. Following the results, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint to $101.1B and lifted adjusted EPS guidance to $11.60-$11.75. Recent clinical developments have added to the company's pipeline momentum. Five-year CARVYKTI data showed treatment-free remission in 50% of patients with early-line relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. TREMFYA also met its primary and major secondary endpoints in the Phase 4 STAR study, while CAPLYTA reported positive Phase 3 results for depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder. These updates reinforce J&J's efforts to expand its oncology, immunology, and neuroscience franchises. Analyst sentiment remains broadly positive. Guggenheim reiterated a Buy rating and $287 price target on October 7, while RBC Capital raised its target to $290, citing pharmaceutical performance, including TREMFYA and Icotyde. JPMorgan raised its target to $285 from $270 while maintaining a Neutral rating. Talc litigation remains a key legal overhang, including a $1.56B Maryland jury verdict that the company plans to appeal. Wall Street rates Johnson & Johnson a Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more cautious at Hold. Also reporting: Citigroup C, Wells Fargo WFC, Goldman Sachs GS, UnitedHealth Group UNH, Domino's Pizza DPZ, Albertsons Companies ACI, and more. Bank of America BAC is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Wednesday, with management's cautious outlook for investment banking fees setting expectations ahead of the release. In Q2 2026, Bank of America reported net income of $9.1B and diluted EPS of $1.21, topping the $1.13 consensus. Revenue rose 19.6% Y/Y to $31.56B, above estimates of $30.78B. Investment banking fees increased 50% Y/Y, trading revenue rose 33%, and return on tangible common equity reached 17%. Management also pointed to continued net interest income (NII) growth, supported by asset repricing and balance-sheet expansion. At the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference in September, CEO Brian Moynihan forecast a decline of at least 10% Y/Y in Q3 investment banking fees to $1.6B-$1.8B from approximately $2B a year earlier. Sales and trading revenue was expected to remain roughly flat against the prior-year quarter's $5.4B. The outlook prompted a 5.1% drop in BAC shares, with trading volume 86% above the three-month average. On October 6, JPMorgan analyst Vivek Juneja lowered his Q3 EPS estimate to $1.12 from $1.16 while maintaining an Overweight rating and a $72 price target. MarketBeat's analyst consensus was Moderate Buy, with an average price target of $63.78. Wall Street rates Bank of America a Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more bullish at Strong Buy. Also reporting: Morgan Stanley MS, ASML Holding ASML, BlackRock BLK, Fastenal FAST, State Street STT, Progressive PGR, and more. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the U.S. market opens on Thursday, with record quarterly revenue already indicated by monthly sales data. Attention is likely to center on the cost of ramping up its 2 nm process, margin trends, and the outlook for continued AI-driven demand. In Q2 2026, TSMC reported revenue of $40.20B, up 36% Y/Y, while EPS of $4.31 beat the $3.82 consensus by 12.8%. Gross margin reached a record 67.7%, operating margin was 60.3%, and net income attributable to shareholders increased 77.4% Y/Y. For Q3, management guided to a revenue of $44.6B-$45.8B, a gross margin of 65%-67%, and an operating margin of 56%-58%, with the anticipated margin decline reflecting the cost of ramping advanced manufacturing nodes. TSMC also raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure outlook to $60B-$64B and increased its revenue growth forecast to above 40% Y/Y from more than 30%. TSMC's latest monthly sales data point to continued momentum. The company reported Q3 revenue of approximately NT$1.49T, up about 39% Y/Y, including September revenue of NT$511.86B, up 54.6%. This puts quarterly sales near the upper end of its guidance range. Industry reports have also pointed to rising customer demand for the 2 nm process family, while Bloomberg reported that TSMC was evaluating a potential semiconductor hub in Texas to complement its planned U.S. manufacturing investments. These developments add to the focus on capacity expansion, advanced-node demand, and the investment required to support future growth. Analyst sentiment remains bullish. Stifel initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $515 price target, while Bernstein reiterated Buy with a $554 target. Morgan Stanley has highlighted the importance of TSMC's 2 nm technology to Apple's upcoming product lineup. Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy consensus on TSM, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more cautious at Hold. Also reporting: Alcoa AA, U.S. Bancorp USB, Ericsson ERIC, Prologis PLD, Charles Schwab SCHW, PNC Financial Services PNC, Interactive Brokers IBKR, J.B. Hunt Transport Services JBHT, Commercial Metals Company CMC, Wipro WIT, and more. The week concludes with a handful of confirmed earnings, including Truist Financial TFC, M&T Bank MTB, Travelers Companies TRV, Regions Financial RF, Citizens Financial Group CFG, and more.
